findings.text: the committed landing record says 'Six cases, 6 passed', but the committed test file holds seven cases and logs/node-tests.log records 7 passed; it also never describes the manifest-commits precondition the shipped rule adds, so a reader of the evidence would not know a delivery naming no commit settles while the obligations still call its review missing. The record understates and partly contradicts the gate it cites.

the added 'if not manifest_commits: return False' precondition narrows the rule beyond the section's deliverable: a scoring run whose manifest names runtime source but omits the commits key still reads review-missing to obligations, yet now settles its pane, so the reflex that would compose that review can still be lost for that population. The plan states no such exemption; it is justified only if the manifest contract guarantees a commits key on every delivery.

item_verdicts.call_sites: The production paths that reach the change are reckon/crew/station.py:512 (the station tick writes the settle reading through live_work_populations) and reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:584,1554 (the fallback settle path through _population_has_live_work).
item_verdicts.diff: Read commit by commit against 97c71c15: one commit, 553 insertions, adding delivered_run_owes_review, its use in live_work_populations, a 451-line seven-case test file and a 54-line evidence fragment.
item_verdicts.done_when: The plan's five cases are all present in tests/test_a_follower_stays_while_a_review_is_owed.py (the two hold cases, both settle-once-stored cases, the tier-none case and the drained case), plus a no-commit case; logs/node-tests.log records 7 passed at 6dedfa1b0c.
item_verdicts.goal: The node goal is to keep a session's follower alive while a delivered run still owes its review; reckon/crew/station_subscriber.py:113-119 now counts such a run in live_work_populations, the one rule both settle paths read.
item_verdicts.manifest: The manifest records status complete, one commit, the node gate 7 passed, base arm 477 passed and head arm 484 passed, both negative controls reproduced, and names logs/node-tests.log; all of those were found on disk.
item_verdicts.write_paths: The commit touches reckon/crew/station_subscriber.py, tests/test_a_follower_stays_while_a_review_is_owed.py and the node's evidence fragment, all inside the manifest's declared orientation_write_paths; crew_follow_commands.py was granted and left untouched.

justifications.durability: restoring the terminal-only rule reddens test_a_station_reading_of_an_owed_review_holds_the_pane and both fallback cases, and dropping the tier check reddens test_a_delivery_that_owes_no_review_settles, each reproduced in logs/negative-control.log.
justifications.evidence: tests/test_a_follower_stays_while_a_review_is_owed.py drives _check_settle through _follow_watch_lines for both settle paths and the tier-none and no-commit exemptions, and logs/node-tests.log records 7 passed while logs/negative-control.log records both controls failing (EXIT=1).
justifications.fit: reckon/crew/station_subscriber.py:103 reaches into the private obligations._review_tier_for_duty across a module boundary and re-spells the classification=='scoring' match rather than calling the duty builder, which couples this module to a private symbol.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/station_subscriber.py:114 counts a terminal pointer back into the live population through delivered_run_owes_review, so a pane stays while the delivered run's review is uncomposed, which is what the node goal names.
justifications.reuse: the change adds no tier or classification rule of its own: it composes recovery.classify_pointer and obligations._review_tier_for_duty, the resolvers the duty and the sweep already use.
justifications.scope_discipline: git show --stat 6dedfa1b0c lists only station_subscriber.py, the new test, and the evidence fragment, every one inside the manifest's orientation_write_paths.
